title: I cut 20 model round-trips to 1 by giving my agent a code sandbox instead of more tools
description:
Every tool call in a standard agent loop is a round-trip to the model. The model calls a tool, the result goes back into context — raw rows and all — and the model samples again. Twenty tools means twenty inferences, and the cost scales with the data.

Programmatic tool calling flips that. Instead of orchestrating each query separately, the model writes code once. That code runs inside a sandbox, executes all the queries against whatever data source it needs, and returns only the final result. The raw rows never touch the context window.

AWS published three implementations of this on Bedrock on May 19: an ECS Docker sandbox, the Agent Core Interpreter, and an Anthropic proxy. The mechanism is the same across all three — the model produces code, the sandbox runs it, one value comes back.

The honest catch: the model has to write correct code. A bug returns a wrong answer with no exception raised. You won't know it failed unless you validate the output externally.

The decision is straightforward: if a data task involves slow or expensive queries, give the model a code sandbox. Don't keep adding individual tools and paying for each round-trip separately.
